final_proof:
Let the sequence of groups defining the direct limit be
\[
G_0 \xrightarrow{f_0} G_1 \xrightarrow{f_1} G_2 \xrightarrow{f_2} \cdots,
\]
and suppose that the homomorphisms \(h_n:G_n\to H\) are compatible with the transition maps, so that
\[
h_{n+1}\circ f_n=h_n \qquad(n\ge 0).
\]
For \(n\le k\), write \(f_{n,k}:G_n\to G_k\) for the composite \(f_{k-1}\circ\cdots\circ f_n\), with \(f_{n,n}=\operatorname{id}_{G_n}\). Iterating the compatibility relation gives
\[
h_k\circ f_{n,k}=h_n. \tag{1}
\]

Recall that \(G_\infty\) consists of equivalence classes of pairs \((x,n)\), where \(x\in G_n\), and
\[
(x,n)\sim(y,m)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\text{for some }k\ge n,m,\quad f_{n,k}(x)=f_{m,k}(y).
\]
We first prove that the formula
\[
h_\infty([(x,n)])=h_n(x)
\]
is independent of the representative. Suppose \((x,n)\sim(y,m)\). Choose \(k\ge n,m\) for which \(f_{n,k}(x)=f_{m,k}(y)\). By (1),
\[
 h_n(x)=h_k(f_{n,k}(x))
       =h_k(f_{m,k}(y))
       =h_m(y).
\]
Thus equivalent pairs have the same image, and hence \(h_\infty\) is a well-defined map \(G_\infty\to H\).

It remains to prove that it is a homomorphism. Let \(a=[(x,n)]\) and \(b=[(y,m)]\), and choose any \(k\ge n,m\). By the definition of multiplication in the direct limit,
\[
ab=\bigl[(f_{n,k}(x)f_{m,k}(y),k)\bigr].
\]
Since \(h_k\) is a group homomorphism and (1) holds,
\[
\begin{aligned}
h_\infty(ab)
 &=h_k\bigl(f_{n,k}(x)f_{m,k}(y)\bigr)\\
 &=h_k(f_{n,k}(x))h_k(f_{m,k}(y))\\
 &=h_n(x)h_m(y)\\
 &=h_\infty(a)h_\infty(b).
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(h_\infty\) is a well-defined group homomorphism.
